1.explanation: This minimal React example uses Carbon’s UIShell SideNav with the `isRail` prop to render it in collapsed/rail mode. We include two SideNavMenu components (each shows its submenu items on hover), plus a SideNavLink for comparison. When you hover over the rail it expands, you then hover on one of the SideNavMenu titles to open its dropdown, and finally you move your mouse into the main content. At that moment the rail collapses back, but the submenu panel remains visible—reproducing the bug exactly as in the screenshot.
1.bug_scenario: When using the Carbon UI Shell’s SideNav in “rail” mode (collapsed by default) with nested menus, you can hover over the rail to expand it, open one of the menu dropdowns, then move the mouse off of the SideNav back into the main content. At that point the rail collapses back to its icon-only state—but the menu panel you opened remains visible and floating, detached from its trigger. This produces the “weird” visual shown in the screenshot.
